title: Pick Any Playing Card in 3 Seconds

visual.description: Close-up of a man's hands performing a high-speed riffle shuffle with a deck of playing cards.

vo.en: Don't blink and don't look away. Just picture one single card floating in total darkness.

visual.description: Extreme macro shot of a man's eye staring intensely with the iris slightly dilating.

vo.en: Lock in the color, the suit, and the number clearly. You think your choice is free, right?

visual.description: A digital stopwatch counting down rapidly with glowing red numbers on a black screen.

vo.en: But here is the creepy part. I already knew which card you were going to choose.

visual.description: A mysterious man's silhouette standing in a doorway with dramatic cinematic backlighting.

vo.en: Over sixty-five percent of people under this rapid pressure choose the Queen of Hearts... or the Ace of Spades.

visual.description: Slow motion shot of the Queen of Hearts and Ace of Spades falling onto a green felt table.

vo.en: It's called psychological priming. Your brain takes the path of least resistance when forced to decide in seconds.

visual.description: A man sitting in a dark library flipping through the pages of a massive psychology textbook.

vo.en: Subscribe for tomorrow's brain hack and comment YES if I caught you. This happens every time you
